args.notes: Array of strings, the program's name excluded.

at.notes: Element `i` of an array, the same as `x[i]`, or code point `i` of a string as a one-character string. A negative `i` counts from the end.

ceil.notes: `x` rounded up to an int. An int is returned unchanged.

code.notes: The code point of a one-character string, as an int.

elapsed.notes: Milliseconds since the program started, as an int. Never decreases.

fields.notes: Frozen array of a record's field names, in literal order (§10.10).

floor.notes: `x` rounded down to an int. An int is returned unchanged.

fromCode.notes: A one-character string holding code point `n`.

get.notes: The value of `k`. Fails if `k` is missing.

isNan.notes: `true` if `x` is `nan`, the only value not equal to itself.

join.notes: The elements as text, converted as interpolation converts them (§9.3), with `sep` between them.

keys.notes: A frozen array of the keys, in order.

length.notes: The number of elements of an array, code points of a string, or keys of a map.

listDir.notes: Frozen array of entry names (not full paths), without `.` and `..`, sorted by code point. Fails if not a directory.

newRandom.notes: A new random number generator, started from an int seed.

pop.notes: Removes the last element of `arr` and returns it. Mutable arrays only; panics if `arr` is empty.

programPath.notes: Absolute path of the file that was launched (see below).

push.notes: Adds `x` at the end of `arr`. Mutable arrays only.

random.notes: A uniformly random int from 0 to `n - 1`. Advances `rng`.

randomFloat.notes: A uniformly random float from `0.0` up to, but not including, `1.0`. Advances `rng`.

readFile.notes: The whole file as a string. Fails if missing or unreadable.

readKey.notes: One key press from stdin, without echo and without waiting for Enter (§12.2). Fails at the end of input.

readLine.notes: One line of stdin, without its line ending. Fails at the end of input.

remove.notes: Removes `k` and returns its value. Fails if `k` is missing. Needs a mutable map.

reverse.notes: A new frozen array of the elements in reverse order.

round.notes: `x` rounded to the nearest int, halves away from zero (`2.5` → 3, `-2.5` → -3). An int is returned unchanged.

run.notes: Runs another program and waits for it. Returns its exit code. Fails if it cannot be started.

slice.notes: The elements or code points from `start` up to, but not including, `end`. Negative indices count from the end. An array result is frozen.

sort.notes: A new frozen array of the elements, sorted by their own values (§10.6).

sortBy.notes: A new frozen array of the elements, sorted by their field named `by`, or by an array `by` of one key for each (§10.6).

split.notes: An array of the parts of `s` between occurrences of `sep`. `""` splits into code points.

terminal.notes: Whether stdin and stdout are terminals, as a record `{ input, output }` of booleans (§12.2).

terminalSize.notes: The size of the terminal on stdout, as a record `{ width, height }` of ints (§12.2). Fails if stdout is not a terminal.

time.notes: Milliseconds since 1970-01-01 00:00 UTC, as an int.

toFloat.notes: The float that number text stands for, such as `"1.5"`. An int is converted, and a float is returned unchanged. Fails on anything else (§9.5).

toInt.notes: The int that integer text stands for, such as `"42"`. An int is returned unchanged. Fails on anything else (§9.5).

toString.notes: The interpolation text of any value that has one (§9.3).

toUint32.notes: The low 32 bits of int `x` as an unsigned int, 0 to 4294967295: an unsigned view of a bitwise result.

trunc.notes: `x` rounded toward zero to an int. An int is returned unchanged.

typeOf.notes: `"int"`, `"float"`, `"boolean"`, `"string"`, `"array"`, `"record"`, `"map"` or `"null"`; for an enum member, the enum's name (§4.1).

values.notes: A frozen array of the values, in the same order as `$keys`.

waitKey.notes: Like `$readKey`, but waits at most `ms` milliseconds: `null` if no key comes in time (§12.2). Fails at the end of input.

writeFile.notes: Creates or overwrites. Fails on error.
